item.title: Kompany improving after collapse but no return date yet — Assistant coach
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany is improving after collapsing during training last week, but there is no confirmed date for his return, assistant coach Aaron Danks has said. According to Reuters, the Belgian was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing during a reserve-team training session. The 40-year-old had been battling a virus and had missed some training sessions in the days leading up to the incident. Danks, who visited Kompany on Monday, said the Bayern manager was in good spirits and appeared to be getting better each day, although there had been no major update on his diagnosis or return to work. “I paid him a short visit yesterday,” Danks told reporters on Tuesday ahead of Bayern’s German Cup second-round match against Magdeburg. “He is in good spirits. It looks like every day he is getting better. There are no major updates in terms of diagnosis or return to work. Let him rest, let him take his time,” he added. Bayern face a demanding run of fixtures in Kompany’s absence, beginning with Wednesday’s German Cup tie against Magdeburg, followed by Saturday’s Bundesliga clash with title rivals Borussia Dortmund. The German champions will then travel to Spain next week to face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Danks said his conversation with Kompany was informal, adding that they avoided discussing football tactics. “We had some good conversations with Kompany but kept it away from football and specific tactics,” he said. “It was just a friendly chat and nice to see him and catch up.” The assistant coach also reflected on an emotional week for Bayern, with Kompany’s health scare coming shortly before striker Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or on Monday. Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the prestigious award, following Michael Owen’s triumph in 2001. Danks said the contrasting events had tested the squad emotionally but praised the team’s unity in dealing with the situation. “For us, we are super professional. Full extremes of life in the last week. Joys and highs for Harry and the lows of the last days,” he said. “To get through these moments we had to rely on our chemistry, our team spirit and that definitely helped us,” Danks added. item.title: Lagos Assembly okays establishment of state police
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou The Lagos State House of Assembly has unanimously supported the proposed establishment of state police following its consideration of the constitutional amendment bill transmitted by the National Assembly. The support was declared by the Speaker of the House, Mr. Mudashiru Obasa, during plenary on Tuesday after the lawmakers reconvened to consider the proposed amendment. The bill, titled *Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Act, 2026*, seeks to provide for the establishment of the State Police Service and related matters. Speaking after reading the relevant sections of the proposed amendment, Obasa said the establishment of state police had remained a recurring issue from the fifth to the 10th Assembly, with successive legislatures deliberating on ways to strengthen security and protect lives and property. He described the development as a step forward but expressed concern that some issues previously raised by state legislatures, particularly those concerning control and the relationship between federal and state police structures, had not been adequately addressed. Obasa said he was pleased that the proposal had received attention, expressing hope that further developments in the amendment process would give states greater control over their policing arrangements. He commended President Bola Tinubu for his commitment to democracy and democratic institutions, as well as the National Assembly, particularly the Senate and the House of Representatives, for their contributions to the constitutional amendment process. The Speaker also commended state Houses of Assembly for supporting the proposal, noting that nearly 25 states had expressed support for the constitutional alteration. However, he stressed the need for clear constitutional provisions defining the functions and responsibilities of state police, warning that disparities in the proposed arrangements could create an imbalance between the federal and state governments. He also called for the establishment of parliamentary police to protect legislative institutions and preserve their independence. Citing past incidents in which state legislative buildings were allegedly demolished or locked up at the instance of governors, Obasa said dedicated parliamentary police would help prevent such occurrences, strengthen state legislatures and safeguard democratic institutions. He expressed confidence that the outstanding concerns would be addressed as the amendment process progressed. Obasa thanked his colleagues for supporting the proposal and urged continued cooperation between the state legislature and the National Assembly to ensure that the remaining issues were resolved. The House subsequently adjourned plenary until November 9, 2026. The post Lagos Assembly okays establishment of state police appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NCDC dismisses Ebola rumours, says no confirmed case in Nigeria
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has dismissed rumours linking the Ebola outbreak to a possible election postponement, saying Nigeria currently has no confirmed cases. The NCDC Director-General, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this at a virtual capacity-building workshop for journalists on effective Ebola reporting on Tuesday in Lagos, warning against misinformation that could undermine containment efforts. Idris said that 54 primary contacts linked to a woman evacuated to Switzerland remained under daily surveillance, in spite of three contacts who developed symptoms last week testing negative for Ebola. He cautioned that the absence of a confirmed case did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, stressing that surveillance and contact tracing must continue until the authorities establish that no further transmission has occurred. “The fact that we currently have no confirmed case does not mean we should declare Nigeria Ebola-free. “We must continue surveillance and ensure that all contacts are properly monitored,” he said. The NCDC boss explained that the woman, whose infection was confirmed on Oct. 20 after she returned to Abuja from Uganda, was evacuated to Switzerland on Oct. 26 alongside her husband at the Swiss Government’s request and expense. He said the patient had improved clinically before her departure, adding that her evacuation should not be interpreted as a vote of no confidence in Nigeria’s healthcare system. Idris said that most of the 54 contacts were quarantined in Abuja, while a few observed self-quarantine at home, adding that surveillance also involved identifying secondary contacts who might have interacted with them. “Three contacts developed symptoms and were tested, but all returned negative results. “However, we cannot stop monitoring them because the results are reassuring,” he said. The NCDC director-general also confirmed approval of ₦100,000 weekly support for quarantined contacts to ease the financial hardship associated with movement restrictions and encourage cooperation with public health authorities. He said the intervention followed concerns about the welfare of affected individuals, noting that the agency was engaging the Federal Capital Territory Administration on its responsibilities towards those under quarantine. Idris urged journalists to verify information through official channels, correct false reports promptly and avoid publishing details that could identify patients or contacts, warning that stigmatisation could harm affected families and healthcare facilities. He reiterated that Ebola spreads through direct contact with the body fluids of an infected person who is sick, not through the air. He advised anyone experiencing fever with relevant travel or contact history to call the designated response hotline, 6232, before visiting a healthcare facility. plenary deliberations on the Constitution Alteration Bill seeking to provide for the establishment of state police across the country. ‎ ‎Yusuf described the passage of the bill as a significant step towards strengthening the country’s security architecture, noting that the growing threats to lives and property required more effective and responsive policing mechanisms. ‎ ‎He identified terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, farmer-herder clashes, political thuggery and other criminal activities as persistent security challenges that had made the need for decentralised policing increasingly urgent. ‎ ‎According to the Speaker, allowing states to establish their own police formations would enable them to respond more quickly to security threats within their jurisdictions. ‎ ‎He explained that state police officers recruited from local communities would have a better understanding of the terrain, residents and peculiar security challenges, enhancing intelligence gathering and the early detection of suspicious movements. ‎ ‎Yusuf recalled that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had initiated the proposed constitutional amendment, which was considered and passed by both chambers of the National Assembly before being transmitted to state Houses of Assembly for consideration in line with Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. ‎ ‎The Speaker said the proposed arrangement would enable state governments to recruit personnel familiar with their communities, thereby improving responses to distress calls and complementing the operations of the Nigeria Police Force. ‎ ‎He added that decentralising policing could reduce administrative delays and improve operational efficiency, particularly in communities where urgent security interventions were required. ‎ ‎Beyond security, Yusuf item.title: 2027: Wike says PDP members across states must support Tinubu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Minister of the Federal Capital Territory Nyesom Wike says he and the Peoples Democratic Party’s National Working Committee have agreed that PDP members in all states must support President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election. Wike made the statement on Tuesday in Rivers State during the unveiling of the Rainbow Coalition’s preferred candidates for the 2027 elections, saying the agreement reflected his position as PDP national leader and the support of the party’s NWC. “What this means is that as the National Leader of the People’s Democratic Party and with the support of the National Working Committee, we have agreed that all the states will support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Wike said. He added that PDP members in several states must support Tinubu, as the Rainbow Coalition aims to unite people across party lines behind the president’s re-election bid. “So, every PDP member in Imo State, you will support Bola Ahmed Tinubu; every PDP member in Kwara, Gombe, Zamfara, Ogun, and all other states must support Bola Ahmed Tinubu as the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.” Wike also said only the party officials he identified and himself could speak on behalf of the PDP, citing the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) recognition of Mao Ohuabunwa as chairman of the party’s Board of Trustees (BOT) and Abdulrahman Mohammed as national chairman. “There is nothing like a factional leader; INEC has recognised the Peoples Democratic Party led by the Mao Ohuabunwa as chairman of the BOT and Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed as the National Chairman, and nobody can speak on behalf of the party except these two people and me, the National Leader,” he added. The coalition unveiled its preferred candidates for the 2027 elections in Rivers, including Kingsley Chinda as its governorship candidate. Rainbow Coalition means no harm, meant to support Tinubu—Wike says, as he calls for united Rivers. Wike also said the Rainbow Coalition was formed to bring people from different political parties together in support of Tinubu. He thanked those who had agreed to work together under the coalition, including the APC governorship candidate, Kingsley Chinda, whom he named as a point of contact. “The candidate of the Rainbow Coalition, let me use as a point of contact, the governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, to appreciate and thank all of you who have agreed to work together, who have agreed under the Rainbow Coalition to support His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, as the president of this country,” Wike said. He said Rivers State was united behind Tinubu and pledged that the state would not return to killings and political crisis. “For those who don’t know, they should know today that Rivers State is entirely for Tinubu. item.title: ‘Wouldn’t be possible without you,’ Kane tells wife after Ballon d’Or win
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has thanked his wife, Katie Goodland, for her support after being named winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or award, declaring that his achievement “wouldn’t be possible without you.” He expressed gratitude to Goodland following the announcement, acknowledging her support throughout his football career as he celebrated one of the sport’s biggest individual honours. Kane, 33, had while receiving the award, spoken for more than 10 minutes, thanking his long-term partner, Goodland, and mother to his four children. “To my wife, Kate, my best friend,” Kane said. “We’ve been through ups and downs for sure. You’re my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself. “The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it’s been horrible for you, here it is – we’ve done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they’re your dreams as well, so it wouldn’t be possible without you. “This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it’s all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you. “Can’t wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you.” The England captain enjoyed an impressive campaign with Bayern Munich last season, playing a key role in the club’s title-winning success and reinforcing his reputation as one of Europe’s leading forwards. He also featured for England at the recently concluded FIFA World Cup, where the Three Lions finished third. Kane emerged ahead of a final three-man shortlist that included France international Kylian Mbappe of Real Madrid and Spanish forward Lamine Yamal of Barcelona. The Ballon d’Or recognises outstanding individual performances in football, with Kane’s contributions at club and international levels placing him among the leading contenders for the award. Kane will now look to build on the achievement as he continues his pursuit of further success with Bayern Munich and England. item.title: Poverty normal globally, not created by Tinubu, says APC spokesperson, Morka
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Spokesperson of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has defended President Bola Tinubu against criticism over poverty and hunger in Nigeria, arguing that successive administrations have failed to eradicate poverty. Morka made the remarks during a RIGHT OF REPLY on ARISE TV, Tuesday, while responding to questions about whether Tinubu was evading responsibility for the country’s economic challenges by describing poverty as a longstanding problem. “Poverty is something that is, you know, a feature of many societies around the globe. Poverty has been with us for a very long time,” he said. The APC spokesman cited the eight years former President Olusegun Obasanjo and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar spent in office together, arguing that they had also failed to eliminate poverty. “Now, in the historical context, Atiku Abubakar was vice president of the Federal Republic for eight years with the former president Olusegun Obasanjo. Now, between the two of them, they had eight years to eradicate poverty, assuming that poverty was that easy to snap your finger and eradicate. Now, let me quickly say that, you know, they didn’t eradicate poverty,” Morka said. He argued that other administrations had similarly failed to eliminate poverty, adding that the challenge could not be resolved simply by political declarations. “All of the other presidents who have come before them did not eradicate poverty, even if we were to suggest that they had a constitutional obligation to eradicate poverty, they didn’t. They couldn’t eradicate poverty,” he said. Morka maintained that Tinubu was therefore correct to refer to the historical context of poverty in Nigeria, rejecting suggestions that the president was using previous administrations to avoid accountability. “So when this president says poverty has been, and, you know, these individuals in their own term of office could have, you know, completely extinguished poverty, take it out. They didn’t. You know, he was saying something that was completely true and not controversial,” he said. He added that opposition figures, including Atiku, were wrong to criticise the president for referring to the past. “So it is only people who simply want to, you know, evade responsibility, like Atiku Abubakar, who will in fact say, you know, why are you referring to the past? Talk about the present,” Morka said. Defending Tinubu’s position, he added: “Listen, there’s no present without the past. The present is only the present because there’s a past, which this president was referring to. So that is not, you know, evading responsibility.” Morka also accused previous administrations of selling off Nigeria’s assets and leaving millions of citizens in poverty, although he did not provide specific details to substantiate the allegation in the interview excerpt. item.title: 2027: INEC chairman tasks staff on neutrality, security, operational readiness
item.description: …Says 13.9m voters in North-East must not be disenfranchised By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, has charged electoral officials across the North-East to uphold strict neutrality, strengthen operational preparedness and ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised in the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the charge on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections held in Gombe State. He said the credibility of the forthcoming elections would depend largely on the professionalism, integrity, punctuality and preparedness of electoral personnel at polling units, ward collation centres and local government offices. The INEC chairman warned that administrative negligence, logistical failures, partisan conduct and poor communication could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and provide opportunities for the spread of misinformation. According to him, the commission’s nationwide readiness assessment was designed to identify operational gaps, assess the preparedness of personnel and strengthen institutional capacity ahead of the elections. Amupitan explained that the North-East engagement followed similar exercises in the South-West, North-West and South-East geopolitical zones, adding that the commission’s leadership had undertaken physical inspections of electoral facilities in Gombe as part of its efforts to evaluate preparedness on the ground. He disclosed that the leadership had visited the palace of the Emir of Gombe, Alhaji (Dr.) Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, and inspected INEC’s zonal store and Gombe Local Government Area office. He said the inspections were necessary to establish the commission’s actual level of preparedness rather than rely solely on administrative reports from headquarters. “The true integrity of an election is not determined in conference rooms in Abuja; it is forged in the field,” Amupitan said, stressing that the conduct of electoral officials at the grassroots would ultimately shape public perceptions of the 2027 polls. 13.9 million voters in North-East. Highlighting the electoral significance of the North-East, the INEC chairman disclosed that the zone accounted for 13,965,475 registered voters across Bauchi, Borno, Adamawa, Taraba, Gombe and Yobe states. The figure, he said, represented approximately 13.51 per cent of Nigeria’s registered voter population of more than 103 million. A breakdown presented at the meeting showed that Bauchi State had 3,012,547 registered voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671. item.title: Reps move to tighten rules for EV, CNG vehicle imports, demand local service centres
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has called for stricter regulations on the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and related equipment, proposing mandatory local maintenance centres, genuine spare parts and after-sales support for importers. The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to establish a transparent licensing framework for companies importing alternative-fuel vehicles, warning against the risk of Nigeria becoming a dumping ground for vehicles without adequate technical support and safety safeguards. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Rep. Ademorin Kuye during Wednesday’s plenary, where lawmakers raised concerns over consumer protection, vehicle safety, local investment and the country’s readiness for the growing adoption of cleaner transportation technologies. Under the proposed framework, the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement, Standards Organisation of Nigeria, Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies, would develop clear criteria for approving importers. Companies seeking approval could be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technicians. Other proposed conditions include investment in electric-vehicle charging stations or CNG refuelling facilities, compliance with national safety and environmental standards, and submission of consumer protection and after-sales service plans. The House also proposed a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and protect consumers. It stressed that the licensing process should be open, competitive and non-discriminatory, allowing all companies that meet the prescribed requirements to obtain approval. The lawmakers further called for tax incentives, import duty concessions and other fiscal benefits to be tied to compliance with the proposed framework to encourage investment in local infrastructure and technical capacity. Contributing to the debate, Rep. Dominic Okafor warned against allowing Nigeria to become a dumping ground for vehicles manufactured without adequate consideration for the needs of developing countries. He said importers must demonstrate their capacity to maintain the vehicles they bring into the country and provide adequate support to consumers after purchase. “It’s very important to see that all the players in this motion are dressed seriously, so that Nigeria is not made a dumping ground,” Okafor said. He observed that some manufacturers produce different categories of vehicles for Western markets and developing countries, including Nigeria, stressing the need for safeguards to ensure that imported vehicles meet local requirements. item.title: Troops repel terrorists in Benue, recover two AK-47 rifles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Maritime Component of Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke have recovered a cache of arms and other items following an intelligence-led operation in Guma Local Government Area of Benue State on 26 October 2026. A statement signed by Lieutenant Ahmad Zubairu Zubairu, Ag Media Information Officer, said the operation followed credible and actionable intelligence indicating that some criminal elements posing as herders had crossed from Nasarawa State into Guma LGA. “On arrival at the location, the troops came under gunfire from the armed group. “The troops responded effectively, repelled the attack and forced the assailants to flee. No casualty was recorded among the troops. Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, four empty AK-47 magazines, eight calves, three mobile phones, a National Identification Number (NIN) document belonging to one Mr Umar Yusuf, and the sum of ₦20 The Force Commander, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke and General Officer Commanding 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Kolo Gara, commended the troops for their vigilance, proactive response and successful recovery of the items. He charged the troops to strengthen collaboration with local communities and sustain intelligence-led operations to prevent criminal activities and enhance security across the Joint Operations Area. Major General Gara also appreciated members of the public for providing credible and actionable intelligence, as well as for the confidence they continue to repose in the troops. He urged residents to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by promptly reporting suspicious movements and activities. item.title: Mbappe apologises for Mao Zedong comment after Chinese sponsors drop him
item.description: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. – Furore – In an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny… but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. China’s foreign ministry said it was aware of the reports regarding Mbappe, who on Monday finished runner-up to English forward Harry Kane in the Ballon d’Or award for the world’s best player. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesm

item.title: ‎US partners with FG to end hunger, starvation
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA – THE Federal Government has received a major boost in its fight against hunger and child malnutrition, with the United States-backed Operation End Starvation (OES) seeking a direct partnership with the Federal Government to help scale up life-saving nutrition interventions across the country. ‎‎The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this in Abuja when he led a delegation from OES and agencies under the Health Ministry to seek collaboration with the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. ‎‎The proposed alliance is expected to strengthen Nigeria’s response to acute child malnutrition, with particular attention to vulnerable children, pregnant women and lactating mothers. ‎‎OES Chief Executive Officer, Williams Holdsworth Moore, said the organisation was impressed by Nigeria’s commitment and the capacity of its health leadership, describing the country as a priority site for its global intervention. ‎‎“We have met with the Nigerian health team, and they are one of the best of many we have met,” Moore said. ‎‎He explained that OES, supported by a macro grant from the United States Government and global philanthropists, plans to channel more than one billion dollars annually towards preventing child deaths caused by starvation. ‎‎“We want to move one billion dollars to end starvation in the next two years across Sub-Saharan Africa. The burden is high, but the capacity is also very high,” he said. ‎‎Moore added that the U.S. State Department had approved Nigeria as part of the organisation’s priority outlook, adding that OES wanted to demonstrate successful large-scale investment through direct government partnership within the next two years. ‎‎He explained thatOperation End Starvation, an initiative of the Eleanor Crook Foundation, is a public-private nonprofit focused on ending child malnutrition and starvation-related deaths across Sub-Saharan Africa, including Nigeria. ‎‎Prof. Pate said Nigeria was already implementing strong frameworks to confront malnutrition, citing the National Community Food Bank Programme, which is being delivered in partnership with the Office of the First Lady. ‎‎He said the programme, recently rolled out across the six geopolitical zones, was already recording positive impact and would be expanded to reach more vulnerable households. ‎‎“Nigeria is working hard to scale down its 6.4 million figure of acute child malnutrition, while also attending to the health of pregnant women and lactating mothers,” Pate said. ‎‎“A lot of good things are already happening in the country.” ‎‎The National Community Food Bank Programme is designed to provide nutritious, locally sourced food to children under six, pregnant women, lactating mothers and other high-risk households through community food banks linked to primary healthcare centres. ‎‎The First Lady of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu welcomed the delegation and commended the quality of expertise and

item.title: Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash – Reports
item.description: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday. Carrick’s future as United manager has been the subject of intense speculation after a run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone. But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine squad session. The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around at Old Trafford following a terrible start to the season. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim. The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League. item.title: Tinubu directs security agencies to arrest killers of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has directed the Nigeria Police and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly and ensure that those behind the murder of prominent Islamic preacher Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, are apprehended and brought to justice. President Tinubu also condemned the dastardly act, describing it as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and the sanctity of human life. The gunmen killed the two men in a drive-by shooting on Monday evening. A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, said: “The President, who was deeply saddened by the news of the killing, described the act as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and the sanctity of human life.” He extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, and the government and people of Katsina State over the tragic loss. According to the statement: “The President has directed the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure the perpetrators are tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice. “President Tinubu prays for the repose of the souls of the departed and for comfort for all those who mourn their deaths.” The post Tinubu directs security agencies to arrest killers of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Edo Voter Register: Utomi, others demand INEC explanation over alleged AI-generated images
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain and economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has raised concerns over allegations that artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs appear in the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) online voter register in parts of Edo State. Utomi’s reaction followed posts by social media user Decosule, who called on INEC to explain the presence of what he described as AI-generated images in voter records displayed on the commission’s website. Decosule shared screenshots purportedly taken from the online voter register for polling units in Ward 11, Etsako West Local Government Area, and Udomi in Esan Central Local Government Area, questioning the authenticity of some photographs. He asked the electoral commission to clarify how the images were included in the register, who conducted the voter registration or image-capturing process, and whether the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) associated with the entries had been collected. In a post reacting to the issue, Utomi warned that questions surrounding the images could undermine public confidence in the country’s electoral process if not properly addressed. “INEC cannot afford to be careless with the credibility of Nigeria’s electoral process. The presence of AI-generated images in a register meant to support our democracy raises serious questions about verification, transparency and accountability. Our democracy is at stake here!” Utomi wrote. Decosule had also claimed to have observed similar images in the register for Udomi in Esan Central, the local government area associated with Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo. The screenshots shared by Decosule showed voter entries under polling units identified as Iyoku–Utukwe Afashio Booth and Ikabigbo I–Ikabigbo Primary School in Etsako West, as well as Udomi Primary School in Esan Central. Decosule urged INEC to provide an explanation, particularly regarding the origin of the photographs and the processes used to verify voter information. However, the screenshots alone do not independently establish that the images were generated using AI or demonstrate whether any irregularities occurred during voter registration. INEC is yet to provide an official response to clarify the authenticity of the photographs, how they came to appear on the online platform and whether the commission had identified any problems with the records. item.title: Mbappe Apologises For Mao Zedong Comment After Chinese Sponsors Dropped Him
item.description: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The paper reported that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Bottles of Dongpeng Beverage Group’s “Bushuila” electrolyte drink featuring French football star Kylian Mbappe on the packaging are displayed at a convenience store in Beijing on October 27, 2026. (Photo by PEDRO PARDO / AFP) | PEDRO PARDO / AFP Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to expand transfer of convicted offenders agreements
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) Act to the House of Representatives for consideration, with a view to extending its application to countries outside the Commonwealth. In a letter dated October 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu urged lawmakers to consider the proposed legislation expeditiously. The bill, titled Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the existing law, Cap. T16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. According to the President, the proposed amendment is designed to give effect to schemes or agreements between the Federal Government of Nigeria and other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders. The amendment would also empower the President, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to extend the application of the Act to any country with which Nigeria has entered into such an agreement. Tinubu said the proposed change would enable Nigeria to implement agreements concluded with countries outside the Commonwealth, potentially broadening the scope of international cooperation on the transfer of convicted offenders. Transmitting the bill pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the President formally requested the consideration of the House of Representatives. “While it is my hope that the House of Representatives will consider this submission expeditiously, please accept, Rt. Hon. Speaker, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu stated in the letter. The bill is now before the House for consideration. The presidential communication did not specify the countries that could be covered by future agreements or provide details of the proposed implementation arrangements.
